title: FOMC decision (meeting Dec 7-8, 2027, with SEP) — decision Wednesday 2027-12-08, 14:00 ET; the year's final meeting and the SEP that sets the 2028 dots
source: EST: federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm, RE-FETCHED DIRECT 2026-09-08 by this session (HTTP 200, 164,831 bytes, page stamp 'Last Update: August 19, 2026') and re-parsed panel by panel rather than inherited from the proposal. The 2027 panel reads verbatim 'January 26-27 | March 16-17* | April 27-28 | June 8-9* | July 27-28 | September 14-15* | October 26-27 | December 7-8*' under the page's own footnote '* Meeting associated with a Summary of Economic Projections' -- December 7-8 CARRIES the asterisk and therefore a SEP, the year's final one. Dec 7 2027 is a Tuesday and Dec 8 a Wednesday, consistent with the two-day convention, and the decision day is the Wednesday. SECOND, NON-FED PRIMARY ON THE SAME DATE: Kalshi's KXFEDDECISION-27DEC event, read direct from the exchange API this session, strikes 2027-12-08T19:00:00Z with contracts closing 18:59:00Z (13:59 ET under EST, one hour later in UTC than the 27OCT contract's 18:00:00Z under EDT -- so the ladder is ET-anchored across the DST boundary, not UTC-anchored). A venue is not a Board primary and promotes nothing; it is an independent statement of the same date. THE PARSE IS ASSERTION-CHECKED before anything downstream is trusted, using the traps the siblings banked: each year panel cut at its own footnote block (the 2027 footnote names a January 25-26, 2028 meeting that a year-scoped parse would return as a phantom ninth 2027 meeting), cross-month labels expanded in both spelled and abbreviated form AND consumed before the same-month pattern runs, and every entry the Board flags itself excluded -- 2020's March 2 (unscheduled), March 15 (unscheduled) and March 17-18 (cancelled), plus 2025's August 22 (notation vote). It returns 167 scheduled meetings, exactly 8 in every year 2007-2027 except 2020's 7, reproducing the sibling assertion exactly. Filed estimate not for want of a primary but because the same page states verbatim 'Each meeting date is tentative until confirmed at the meeting immediately preceding it' -- the confirming venue is the 2027-10-26/27 meeting, the proposing lane's own event, not a better fetch. The 14:00 ET statement time is the standing convention and is not on this page. Checked 2026-09-08
notes: CANONICAL FILE written by the fomc-2027-12-08 initial-research lane (2026-09-08) after reading the one prior proposal, proposals/fomc-2027-12-08.from-fomc-2027-10-26.json, which is now inert. Every date claim it made was re-derived from the primaries rather than inherited and held; ONE STATISTICAL CLAIM DID NOT. THE COMMISSION THIS ENTRY ARRIVED WITH, AND ITS ANSWER: the proposal instructed whoever drew this id to test 'December carries the HIGHEST monthly mean absolute S&P decision-day move in the table, 1.265% at n=19 ... whoever researches this id should test it before quoting it, because the two cells this family has tested both failed.' Tested on 156 FOMC decision days 2007-2026 from CBOE SPX_History.csv (13,028 bars to 1975), and it fails THREE WAYS. (1) IT IS NOT THE HIGHEST CELL -- August is, at 1.482% on n=7, a figure that appears in the proposer's own quoted table, so this is arithmetic rather than a new measurement; December is rank 2 and the defensible claim is only 'the largest cell with n>=11'. (2) IT IS A ONE-PRINT CELL -- 2008-12-16 (+5.136%) is the largest absolute decision-day move in the whole 156-day sample, and dropping it alone takes December to 1.050% while December-vs-rest goes from P=0.0896 to P=0.4424; the sign test never supported it (12 of 19 above the rest-of-calendar median, P=0.18). (3) SELECTION-CORRECTED IT IS NOTHING, AND SO IS THE REST OF THE TABLE -- December was quoted BECAUSE it topped a twelve-cell table, so the honest test is a max-statistic permutation: P(max of 12 relabelled cells >= December's 1.265) = 0.8212, and at the table's true maximum, August's 1.482, P = 0.4076. The entire 2.8x spread from June's 0.522 to August's 1.482 is what twelve random cuts of 156 observations look like. THE DEPLOYABLE CONCLUSION IS THEREFORE A RETIREMENT, NOT A FOURTH CORRECTION: September's cell was corrected as a mixture and October's as a bin split, both of which left the table standing and implicitly licensed the other cells; no cell in it is quotable, and the prior for any FOMC decision session is the pooled 0.925% mean / 0.650% median. THE ONE RESULT THAT LOOKED REAL IS RECORDED WITH ITS OWN EXECUTION ATTACHED: December decision days run 1.265% against 0.710% for an ordinary December session (ratio 1.78, permutation P=0.0135), and it is the only statistic in the document that gets STRONGER when 2008 is removed (1.050 vs 0.624, P=0.0074) and holds in the modern era (1.092 vs 0.618, P=0.0102), while non-December decision days do not beat their own months (P=0.354) and ordinary December sessions are themselves quiet (0.710 vs 0.801, P=0.072) -- BUT that contrast was found by running twelve of them, and P(max of the 12 month-contrasts >= December's +0.555) = 0.438. Registered as a forward test, not asserted. THE SEP IS REFUTED AS THE MECHANISM: SEP-month decision days (Mar/Jun/Sep/Dec, n=77) 0.989% vs non-SEP (n=79) 0.862%, P=0.405, and June is a SEP meeting and the quietest cell in the table at 0.522%.
